name: d2
desc: Modern diagram scripting language that turns text to diagrams
why: Diagram scripting language is a neat text-to-picture transform, but it is popular and mostly a diagram tool.

brief.what_it_is: D2 is an open-source command-line tool and Go library that turns text written in its own declarative diagram language into diagrams. You write a .d2 file describing shapes, containers, and arrows, and the d2 command renders it to SVG, PNG, PDF, PPTX, GIF, or ASCII. It bundles three layout engines and a built-in autoformatter, and it can watch a file and live-reload a browser preview as you edit. The homepage also describes an online playground and editor extensions for VS Code, Vim, and Obsidian.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to "get a mental model from your head onto the screen, then make edits with your team" with simple syntax and no drag-and-drop diagram editor. The README calls it "A modern diagram scripting language that turns text to diagrams."
brief.how_it_works: A .d2 file is parsed into a graph of shapes, containers, and connections, with variables, imports, and globs for reuse. The chosen layout engine (dagre by default, elk, or the opt-in tala) positions the nodes, and the renderer writes the result as SVG or another export format. Sketch mode, LaTeX labels, and fonts are handled by bundled Go ports of rough.js, MathJax, and Source Sans Pro-based rendering.

brief.install_notes: The README's primary path is the curl-to-shell install script, which the README itself says to pair with a review of its behavior (--dry-run). It also says the OS package manager is preferred for security, and the homepage says D2 is included in Homebrew and Winget. Installing from source needs Go; precompiled binaries are on the GitHub releases page; a release-from-source route with manpages is documented in docs/INSTALL.md. The README says D2 needs no browser to run and can work entirely server-side, and no account is mentioned. Fonts can be swapped by supplying your own .ttf files. Editor support needs the separate VS Code or Vim extensions.
brief.standout: The homepage claims D2 is the only text-to-diagram language that can produce animated diagrams, and it also advertises a hand-drawn sketch mode and an offline CLI with watch mode. Its layout engines are native Go ports (dagre, elk, and the TALA engine aimed at software architecture diagrams), so the tool needs no external runtime. The README also lists a large community ecosystem of plugins, including Pandoc filters, MkDocs, VitePress, and a Postgres ERD importer.
brief.status: Maintained, with evidence but no dates. The README shows active CI, a weekly race-test workflow, a release badge, a changelog, and a next.md file for upcoming changes. The homepage is a current docs site with a Discord and blog. I did not see a last-release date or last-commit date, so I cannot give an exact date.
brief.caveats: The install script is curl piped to sh; the README itself recommends the package manager for better security. The README says D2 makes no network connection after installation, except for periodic version checks against GitHub. TALA is bundled but opt-in. The README says the editor extensions for VS Code and Vim exist, but the homepage says the Vim and VS Code support has 'more coming soon,' so coverage may be incomplete. The license is Mozilla Public License 2.0. The 'only language that can animate diagrams' claim is the project's own marketing statement and I did not verify it against other tools.
